subject.title: Feature Request: AI Screen Sharing Capability

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a consent-first screen-sharing capability as a core product program, and if so what initial client, provider, transport, privacy, and data-retention scope is acceptable?
rationale: The request introduces a new sensitive-data capture workflow across multiple product surfaces; code review cannot safely choose its product boundary or privacy contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Defer implementation pending a scoped design
options.body: Keep this request as the umbrella discussion and require an owner-approved consent, privacy, transport, and platform MVP before opening implementation work.

options.title: Sponsor a browser-only MVP
options.body: Define an explicitly consented WebChat-only still-frame or low-rate capture flow first, with visible sharing state, stop controls, provider restrictions, and a reviewed data-handling contract.

options.title: Route transport exploration first
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89131 to evaluate a generic provider/gateway frame contract, while keeping screen capture and client UX out of scope until separately approved.

recommendation.title: Defer implementation pending a scoped design
recommendation.body: Keep this request as the umbrella discussion and require an owner-approved consent, privacy, transport, and platform MVP before opening implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most directly connected person in the available evidence through the active adjacent transport-design proposal; product sponsorship still requires an appropriate repository decision-maker.
